- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.44 or higher) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate when sentiment is mildly negative (e.g., -0.08 to 0.09) — model ignores downward pressure, especially near end of forecast horizon.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts 2–3 days too late to sentiment changes, especially when sentiment turns positive.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to adjust downward when sentiment cools or stabilizes.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate later periods (especially 20–30 days out) — model assumes momentum persists longer than it does.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model overcorrects and then underestimates the next spike — creates “double dip” error pattern.
- Avoid extrapolating from 18-day history — model overfits recent trends and ignores sentiment decay or reversal signals.
